knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement gives the expectation and variance of aX+bY?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Expectation is linear. Variance squares scale coefficients and includes the covariance cross-term.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Dropping covariance without independence or failing to square variance coefficients.

choices.label: Var(aX+bY)=aVar(X)+bVar(Y)+2abCov(X,Y), because variance is linear in constants.
Var(aX+bY)=a²Var(X)+b²Var(Y) for all X and Y, because covariance never affects a linear combination.
E[aX+bY]=a²E[X]+b²E[Y], matching the squared coefficients used in variance.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Var(X)=4, Var(Y)=9, and Cov(X,Y)=2. What is Var(2X-Y)?
knowledge_checks.body: Compute the variance with its covariance term.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: With a=2 and b=-1, the cross-term is negative: 2abCov=-8.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Dropping covariance for dependent variables or losing the negative coefficient in the cross-term.

choices.label: Var(2X-Y)=16+9=25 because covariance is omitted whenever the variables differ.
Var(2X-Y)=2(4)-9+2(2)(-1)(2)=-9 because variance follows the signs in the linear combination.
Var(2X-Y)=16+9+8=33 because covariance always enters with a positive sign.
